newsitem.title: UK: BA says lost tens of millions from strike.
newsitem.headline: BA says lost tens of millions from strike.

text.p: British Airways Plc chief executive Robert Ayling on Tuesday told the annual meeting that last week's strike had cost the company "tens of millions of pounds" and he urged the main cabin crew union involved in the dispute to adopt a "constructive approach".

He welcomed the decision by the main union representing catering workers to drop the threat of a strike and to accept the company's offer for further talks on the sale of its catering business at London Heathrow airport.

"Modern trade unionism is about working together with management in the interests of the business as a whole. I hope and believe that BASSA (the BA cabin crew union) will come to share that view by joining a programme of improved competitiveness with which the great majority of employees have already agreed," Ayling told the meeting.
BA is currently waiting for BASSA to supply it with proposals on how to achieve 42 million pounds ($70.9 million) of savings following last week's 72-hour strike by cabin crew.
"This dispute is not about union busting. I have no plans to de-unionise British Airways, though many of newer airline competitors have no unions at all," Ayling said.
Ayling added that any business that becomes enmeshed in internal disputes will lose ground to its competitors.
The cabin crew unions have objected to BA imposing pay and conditions on them without consultation.
